issues.title: Daily Early Years Cap
issues.headline: BAT AND ARM: RILE'S TWO-WAY WEEK
issues.dek: Ed Rile hit .316/.346/.421 and posted a 1.32 ERA over 88.2 innings as the Day-Trippers went 14-7; final result: out in round four (3rd-4th of 32).
issues.park: 1890 Exposition Park III (from the tournament catalog, read 2026-10-14)
lead: Some clubs carry a hitter and a pitcher. This one carried Ed Rile. At the plate: .316/.346/.421 (OPS+ 153) and 18 RBI in 81 plate appearances. On the mound: 10 starts, 7-3, a 1.32 ERA over 88.2 innings (ERA+ 231), 73 strikeouts and 9 walks. He is listed twice in the box score, and neither listing is a misprint.

Most of the bracket was already home when this one ended. Put Dock Ellis Day-Trippers down for 14-7 in the Daily Early Years Cap: 310 runs scored, 52 allowed, 21 games, 14.8 and 2.5 a game. By adjusted run difference they ranked 7th of 32. Final result: out in round four (3rd-4th of 32).
Hitters did a lot of walking back to the dugout. The staff struck out 6.7 per nine (bracket 4.9) and walked 0.7.
There was no soft spot to pitch around. 11 of 12 regulars with 40 or more plate appearances ended at OPS+ 120 or better.
The margin: 258 runs better than the opposition over 21 games, 12.3 a game.

Ed Delahanty set the tone, hitting .432/.485/.693 (OPS 1.178, OPS+ 287) with 3 home runs over 99 plate appearances. Dave Bancroft chipped in too, with an OPS+ of 235 and 1 home run. Somebody has to cash them in, and Dave Bancroft did: 34 RBI, 9 doubles.
They ran, too. The Day-Trippers finished with 27 steals, caught 14 times, in 21 games, the 3rd-highest rate of steals a game among the bracket's 32 clubs. Charlie Smith led with 5.
Mordecai Brown followed him in the rotation with a 2.11 ERA over 94.0 innings.
"That one stings," said bench coach Lefty Mahoney. "A good sting. If there is such a thing."

issues.title: Daily Iron Strikes Back
issues.headline: SMITH'S WEEK: OPS+ 149 AS DAY-TRIPPERS GO 18-11
issues.dek: An OPS+ of 149 over 107 plate appearances for Ozzie Smith; the Day-Trippers went 18-11; final result: out in round five (3rd-4th of 64).
issues.park: 1990 Anaheim Stadium (from the tournament catalog, read 2026-10-14)
lead: The week belonged to one man, and his name was Ozzie Smith. In 107 plate appearances he hit .326/.421/.461 (OPS .881, OPS+ 149) with 2 home runs, 6 doubles, 21 RBI and 13 runs scored, walking 16 times and striking out 9. He hit 2 of the club's 21 home runs and drove in 21 of its 132 runs. The Dispatch's scout, who is invented, stopped taking notes in the third game and just watched.

It was a run. It just was not the whole run. The Dock Ellis Day-Trippers ended at 18-11 in the Daily Iron Strikes Back, with 132 runs scored and 99 allowed across 29 games, 4.6 for and 3.4 against a game. By adjusted run difference they ranked 5th of 64. Final result: out in round five (3rd-4th of 64).
The late innings were an adventure: 2 blown saves in 12 chances. Of 25 inherited runners, 2 scored.
The ball stayed in the park: 21 home runs in 29 games, 0.72 a game, in a bracket that hit 1.11.

Start with the pitching, because the pitching started everything. TJ House made 5 starts with a 2.12 ERA over 34.0 innings (ERA+ 183), 7.9 strikeouts per nine. Behind him, Nathan Eovaldi added a 2.64 ERA in 47.2 innings. The strikeout lead went to James McDonald, with 41 against 9 walks in 37.1 innings.
When the phone rang in the bullpen, it was usually for John Bale: 1.45 ERA over 18.2 innings (ERA+ 268) and 8 saves.
Behind him, Santiago Espinal posted an OPS+ of 144 with 2 home runs in 103 plate appearances.
They ran, too. The Day-Trippers finished with 8 steals, caught 2 times, in 29 games. Ozzie Smith led with 4.
"We were in every game," said bench coach Lefty Mahoney. Then, after a pause: "Most of them."

lead: They will be telling this one at the hotel bar for a while. Put Dock Ellis Day-Trippers down for 19-2 in the Daily Around the Horn Before Bed: 304 runs scored, 50 allowed, 21 games, 14.5 and 2.4 a game. By adjusted run difference they ranked 2nd of 64.
Both halves of the roster earned their meal money: 14.5 runs a game scored and 2.4 allowed, in a bracket that averaged 5.9.
There was no soft spot to pitch around. 10 of 10 regulars with 40 or more plate appearances ended at OPS+ 120 or better.

The hitters will get their paragraph. First, Dave Stieb. He made 5 starts and went 4-0 with a 1.21 ERA over 37.1 innings: 42 strikeouts, 7 walks, 15 hits and 5 earned runs allowed, a 0.59 WHIP. He finished 1 of the starts himself. Only 2 of the bracket's 58 arms with 15 or more innings had a better ERA+. The radar gun operator asked for the afternoon off. There was nothing left to measure.

The lineup card had Derrek Lee on it every day for good reason. He hit .506/.593/.885 (OPS 1.478, OPS+ 272) with 5 homers in 113 trips. Right behind him, J.D. Martinez posted an OPS+ of 212 with 6 home runs. Lee led the club with 44 RBI.
On the bases, the Day-Trippers stole 18 and were caught 2 times in 21 games, the highest rate of steals a game among the bracket's 64 clubs. Mike Trout had 5 of them.
Mike Scott followed him in the rotation with a 1.79 ERA over 40.1 innings.
"Pitching and defense," said bench coach Lefty Mahoney, chewing on something he would not identify. "And about six home runs a night."
